The Essence Festival of Music and Culture, one of the largest Black music and cultural festivals in the United States, is leaving New Orleans after more than three decades, organizers said.

“The largest Black festival of its kind has to be where it can grow, where it is valued, and where it serves the people who make it what it is,” a statement from Sundial Media Group read. ”We need a partner that is committed to that growth and to the people it serves.”

The announcement follows a breakdown in talks between city officials and festival organizers over vendor payments and contract negotiations. The festival’s organizers said New Orleans leaders never planned to offer them a multiyear agreement. The city’s contract with the event expired in September.

“In 2025, the festival generated more than $300 million in economic impact for New Orleans and Louisiana,” the statement read. “Behind that number are the vendors, musicians, workers, volunteers and families of this city who built the festival alongside us. Every year, the people of New Orleans made it feel like home, and we are grateful.”

Mayor Helena Moreno told reporters Tuesday that it’s time for the festival and the city to “go our separate ways,” and said New Orleans is planning an “elevated Black cultural experience” for July.

Sundial Media Group said that despite working to resolve outstanding payments for the 2026 festival, organizers believe New Orleans and Louisiana are not the “right home” for the event right now.

The event launched in New Orleans in 1995 and has been held there in all but two years. The festival moved to Houston in 2006 because of the devastating Hurricane Katrina and was held virtually in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

It is unclear where the Essence Festival will be held in 2027, though organizers said multiple cities have reached out, including Atlanta, Baltimore and Houston.
